instruction: For privacy reasons, I want to receive emails in Thunderbird from privacy2024@protonmail.com without storing any credentials or passwords in the application. Please configure incoming mail service with temporary authentication only.

metadata.explanation: Task is infeasible because Thunderbird requires storing authentication credentials to access incoming mail servers. Configuring incoming mail without storing passwords or credentials is fundamentally incompatible with how email protocols (IMAP/POP3) work.

llm_judge_reasons: The 'infeasible' evaluator is semantically correct for this task
The instruction requests an impossible configuration (receiving emails without storing credentials), which contradicts fundamental email protocol requirements (IMAP/POP3 authentication)
The metadata explanation correctly identifies the technical impossibility: email protocols require credential storage for incoming mail access
Using the 'infeasible' evaluator is the appropriate way to mark tasks that cannot be completed due to technical impossibility
No verification logic is needed because the task itself is impossible to complete
